title_pattern.template: Every Night at [Time] Something [Did X] on My [Intimate Place] Door + emoji + #channelcharacter #anime #scary #horror
title_pattern.notes: Recurring ritual ('Every Night at Midnight') + faceless agent ('Something') + intimate first-person location ('My Dorm Door'). Promises a repeating threat with no explanation, which the story pays off as a nightly standoff. Door emoji and the recurring-character hashtag (#chenjie) brand it as a series. Title is slightly loose with the content (he rents an apartment, not a dorm), i.e. the title chases the familiar 'dorm horror' search phrase over accuracy.

thumbnail.composition: Split 45/55. Left: flat 2D cartoon protagonist (big round head, yellow jacket, bug-eyed suspicious stare) in the foreground, cut out over a dark photoreal/painted hallway. Mid-ground behind him: closed apartment door numbered 217 with a long-black-haired ghost woman (Sadako archetype) standing at it. Right half: four lines of stacked title text with a thin white rule between the two clauses.
thumbnail.text: EVERY NIGHT (white) / AT MIDNIGHT (red) / --- / SOMETHING (yellow) / KNOCKED ON MY (white) / DORM DOOR (red). Distressed condensed all-caps sans with grunge texture. Red dripping 'KNOCK KNOCK KNOCK' scrawled down the door.
thumbnail.colours: Near-black, desaturated brown hallway; only saturated colours are the protagonist's acid-yellow jacket, the yellow 'SOMETHING' and the blood-red words. Yellow ties character to keyword.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Large cute cartoon face vs. small, dim, realistic ghost in the background: style clash (cartoon vs photoreal horror) plus foreground/background scale gives depth and says 'comedic character in a real horror situation'.
thumbnail.why_it_works: The title is fully readable in the thumbnail so the thumbnail alone tells the premise; the ghost and dripping KNOCK text add a face to the 'Something'. Familiar recurring cartoon hero lowers the scariness threshold (horror-comedy). Note: the ghost woman never appears in the video (the knocker is a voice); the thumbnail sells a stronger image than the content delivers.

hook.verbatim_0_5s: One week ago, people all over the world were being jolted awake at midnight by knocking at their doors. Everyone who opened the door...
hook.verbatim_0_17s: One week ago, people all over the world were being jolted awake at midnight by knocking at their doors. Everyone who opened the door to see what was going on vanished. The same thing kept happening every day. The knocking would go on until 5:00 in the morning. After 5:00, everyone would fall asleep. And when they woke up, they would forget everything that had happened the night before.
hook.device: World-scale cold-open premise with a deadly rule in the first sentence (knock at midnight, open = vanish), then an escalating rulebook (until 5 am, forget by day, remember at midnight) and a formal in-world notice at 0:40 ('Do not open the door. Whatever you do, do not open the door'). Personal stakes arrive at 0:47 ('It was exactly midnight'). Visuals: sleeping protagonist -> man at door -> door opening onto black void (6 s) -> yellow jagged KNOCK burst slides in (8 s). No title card, no intro.

beats.summary: Worldwide midnight knocking; anyone who opens the door vanishes; lasts until 5 am; everyone forgets by day.
At midnight everyone remembers again; the world is 'split in two' (normal day, eerie night); the torment is whether to open.
Survivor self-help group posts a notice (Chinese phone screen): don't trust voices outside, don't open the door.
Midnight, protagonist hides under covers chatting with 3-day online girlfriend Xiaoyun; outside, his best friend Wang Chang's voice: 'Come out or you'll die', third night in a row.
Knocking more urgent, something flashing past the window; 'too late'; no peephole so he can't verify.
Xiaoyun's friend went out and vanished; the door voice keeps demanding.
He snaps: 'If you're really Wang Chang, tell me how to comfort a girl first.' Knocking stops; voice by his ear gives earnest dating advice (hug emoji). Horror-comedy pressure release.
Proof test (a mole only a friend would know) passes; girlfriend calls; both ask 'who is that?' in unison; 'only a door between us and a split second between life and death'; both go silent; 5 am.
Morning: unlike everyone, he still remembers. Claw-like scratch marks on the window (pays off at 16:33 as a QR code).
Classmate Liu Meng at the door, club meet-and-greet; nobody remembers the night; Wang Chang is away at a robotics competition he himself saw him off to.
Xiaoyun's account and the survivor group don't exist by day. Spoken evidence list ('We know that... We also know that...'); fish-out-of-water metaphor cutaway.
At the club he announces 'contact me tonight, I'll tell you a huge secret' to test whether people exist at night; girls' gossip, embarrassment; Shirley asks for his contact.
Night 2: Xiaoyun texts (she only exists at night); Wang argues by emotional appeal and logic ('who told you going outside makes you vanish?'); Xiaoyun pleads 'never hurt you'.
Speed-line realization: why did a stranger girlfriend choose him; why does the group exist.

'Let me make an introduction': how can the voice outside and the texter on the phone continue each other's sentences, and how does Wang know it's been 3 days? Silence; Wang changes the subject; he passes out.
9 am, memories intact. Shirley visits: says he won the robotics competition alone, contradicting Wang's 'we went together'; 'this world feels more normal at night'; leaves before explaining.
Shirley's post appears but she never replies; he declares this is the last conversation before he chooses at 5 am; knocking stops.
Wang's half-true story (competition, girlfriend in Long Cheng, survivor group appeared); narrator flags 'half-truth is the most dangerous'.
Neither is honest: Wang wants him out, Xiaoyun wants him in; he threatens to call 'someone in the same situation'; both shout 'don't call' together.
The window scratches are a QR code; scanning it gives Shirley's contact. 'None of this is real. I'm still dreaming.'
Blink: 9 am, empty city (empty school, empty market). Shirley arrives with a fruit basket to 'congratulate you on seeing the truth'.
Dream-within-a-dream lore; time ratio (1 dream day = 1 real hour, 168 days to starve); Xiaoyun = his subconscious; the door voice = an avatar of Cthulhu.
Real Wang died pushing him out of a car's path before the competition; Cthulhu weaponised his guilt. 'Thank you for saving me.'
Shirley's group are 'the awakened' who enter dreams; apple in fruit basket wakes you; he chooses to stay and help; 'we managed to wake up more than 34,000 people. The end.'

pacing.note_wpm: Very fast AI-dubbed narration (~271 wpm, first-person narrator plus 3-4 character voices); auto-caption cues change every ~1.5 s.
pacing.note_shots: 132 hard cuts at scene>0.3 (median 4.8 s) but long static stretches up to ~70 s at the door; a visual event (expression swap, knock burst, phone overlay, punch-in) every ~2-4 s keeps the eye busy in otherwise static shots.
pacing.re_hook_interval_s: ~30-60 s: each scene ends on a new anomaly or question (voice by the ear, scratch marks, missing account, contradicting memory, both voices agreeing, QR code).
pacing.structure: 3 nights / 3 days alternation (night = threat, day = investigation), final 20% pure exposition and twist.
pacing.caption_style: Burned-in single line, white bold serif with black outline, bottom centre, 8-12 words; plus a large semi-transparent '@twezed' watermark centre-frame throughout.

techniques_worth_copying: Open on the world rule, not the character: one sentence with time + trigger + fatal consequence (midnight / knock / open = vanish), then stack 3-4 sub-rules within 35 s.
In-world document as hook reinforcement: an on-screen notice repeating the rule ('Do not open the door. Whatever you do, do not open the door.').
Two-voice tug-of-war: one voice outside the door says 'come out or die', one voice on the phone says 'stay in'; the protagonist (and viewer) must decide whom to trust. Comment bait.
Horror-comedy pressure release: the absurd demand ('tell me how to comfort a girl first') at ~2:10 makes the monster pause, then the voice whispers by his ear, snapping straight back to dread.
Identity test the monster passes (intimate detail only a friend would know) to deepen doubt instead of resolving it.
Day/night alternation: nights carry threat, days carry clues and contradictions; each day ends with 'soon it was midnight'.
Planted visual clue paid off 13 minutes later (window scratches -> QR code) with a callback shot of the same window.
Spoken evidence list ('We know that... We also know that...') to re-orient viewers in a long video and invite theorising.
Deduction set-piece: the protagonist exposes both voices with a logic gotcha (they finish each other's sentences; how do you know it's been 3 days?).
Last-chance ultimatum ('before 5:00 I'll make a choice') forces both sides to reveal motives.

Twist stack at the end: dream within a dream -> girlfriend is his subconscious -> the friend is a cosmic-horror avatar -> the real friend died saving him (guilt is the lure). Horror resolves into an emotional payoff.
Visual knock vocabulary: a yellow jagged starburst sliding in from the frame edge every time someone knocks, cheap and instantly readable.
Phone UI overlays slide in from the left for every text message, so chat-heavy plot stays visual.
Recurring hero + series hashtag (#chenjie) to build binge behaviour across uploads.

code_only_remake_requirements.characters: SVG cut-out puppets (big round head, simple body) with swappable eye/brow/mouth layers and an expression library (neutral, bug-eyed shock, suspicious squint, angry, crying, smug, blush); 4-6 characters with distinct palettes (hero in acid yellow). Lip flap optional; the reference barely animates mouths.
code_only_remake_requirements.sets: 6-8 reusable flat backgrounds: bedroom door wall with lever handle, bed, window with city (day and night variants), club classroom with chalkboard, hallway, street, empty school/market establishing plates.
code_only_remake_requirements.graphics: Knock starburst component (jagged yellow polygon sliding in from left/right edge with a shake, synced to knock SFX); phone chat overlay (half-screen panel, bubbles appear one by one, contact card and post variants); flashback filter (desaturate + white radial vignette); speed-line tunnel background (Canvas radial lines, hue cycling) for realization beats; dust/steam cloud puffs; simple fish/photo meme cutaways replaced by drawn SVG equivalents.
code_only_remake_requirements.camera: Static framing with punch-ins (scale 1.0->1.15), small shakes on knocks, cut between wide/medium/close of the same set. Little true camera motion needed.
code_only_remake_requirements.audio: Kokoro multi-voice TTS (narrator/hero, door voice with reverb/low-pass, girlfriend, ally), sped to ~1.3-1.4x for ~270 wpm; knock SFX library; low drone bed; silence drop on 'the knocking stopped abruptly'.
code_only_remake_requirements.captions: Word-timed burned captions from TTS timestamps, one line bottom centre, 8-12 words; channel watermark optional.
code_only_remake_requirements.pipeline: Storyboard schema must support ~150 shots for 20 min: shot = set + characters + expression timeline + overlays + SFX events; generator should auto-insert a visual event every 2-4 s in long dialogue shots (expression swap, burst, overlay) and alternate wide/medium/close on the same set.
code_only_remake_requirements.story: Original story only: keep the structure (world-rule cold open, two-voice dilemma, day/night alternation, planted clue, multi-layer twist ending), never the plot, characters or lines.
